head: It never made a chip.
Its designs are everywhere.
slides.sub: How a tiny team near Cambridge licensed its way into phones.

image.label: A glowing microchip blueprint on a drafting table
image.brief: 어두운 사무실 제도용 책상 위에서 빛나는 마이크로칩 설계도. 공장도 기계도 없이 종이와 선만 있는 구도. 실제 로고 없음.

head: A computer maker’s
side project.
body: In the 1980s, Acorn Computers in Cambridge designed its own processor, the ARM, for its desktop machines. It was simple and used very little power.
A story often told: an early test chip kept running even when its power supply wasn’t properly connected.

image.label: A 1980s British computer lab with beige machines
image.brief: 1980년대 영국 케임브리지의 컴퓨터 연구실. 베이지색 데스크톱, 회로 기판, 흐린 창밖. 인물은 뒷모습 실루엣. 실제 브랜드 디자인 없음.

slides.label: engineers who left Acorn to start the new company in 1990
body: Advanced RISC Machines was a joint venture of Acorn, Apple and chipmaker VLSI Technology. Apple wanted a low-power chip for its Newton handheld. The team reportedly started out in a converted barn.

image.label: A converted English barn used as an office
image.brief: 영국 시골의 개조한 헛간 사무실. 나무 들보 아래 책상과 컴퓨터 몇 대. 1990년대 초 분위기.

head: Big ambitions.
No factory.
body: A chip plant cost far more than a startup could ever raise. The biggest chipmakers had giant factories and decades of scale.
Robin Saxby, who became CEO in 1991, had a small team, one main customer and limited cash.

image.label: A huge chip factory seen from far away at night
image.brief: 밤에 멀리서 본 거대한 반도체 공장. 불 켜진 클린룸 창. 작은 헛간 사무실과 대비되는 규모감.

head: No money for a factory.
How do you compete?
body: You have a strong, low-power chip design and very little cash. The giants own the factories.

options.text: License the design to chipmakers for a fee, plus a royalty on every chip
options.feedback: You earn little at first and depend on your partners selling well. Keep swiping.

options.text: Raise money and make your own chips to sell, like the big players
options.feedback: You keep the full profit on each chip, but need huge capital and must beat giants at manufacturing. Keep swiping.

options.text: Work only for Apple as its dedicated chip team
options.feedback: Steady income, but your fate rides on one customer’s products. Keep swiping.

image.label: A crossroads of three paths drawn as circuit lines
image.brief: 회로 선으로 그려진 세 갈래 길. 어두운 배경에 금색 선. 추상적 그래픽.

head: Sell the blueprint,
not the chip.
body: Arm licensed its designs to semiconductor companies. Each paid an upfront fee, then a small royalty on every chip shipped. Partners added their own parts, made the chips and sold them.
Arm owned no factories, and it didn’t compete with its customers.

image.label: One blueprint being copied to many different factories
image.brief: 설계도 한 장에서 여러 갈래 빛줄기가 뻗어 각기 다른 공장으로 향하는 구도. 로고 없음.

head: Then phones needed
batteries that last.
body: In the 1990s, Texas Instruments used an Arm design in chips for mobile phones, including Nokia handsets. Low power mattered more than raw speed.
Each new licensee brought more software and tools, which drew in the next. Arm listed in London and on Nasdaq in 1998.

image.label: A late-1990s mobile phone on a café table
image.brief: 1990년대 후반 카페 탁자 위의 작은 휴대전화. 따뜻한 조명. 실제 제품 디자인과 로고는 따라 하지 않음.

slides.label: what SoftBank agreed to pay for Arm in 2016
body: By then, partners were shipping billions of Arm-based chips a year, inside nearly every smartphone. The company that never made a chip had become one of Britain’s biggest tech businesses.

image.label: A city skyline at night filled with glowing phone screens
image.brief: 밤의 도시 풍경 속 수많은 스마트폰 화면 불빛. 2010년대 분위기. 인물은 실루엣.

head: Own the design.
Let others carry the cost.
body: Factories are costly and risky. By licensing, Arm turned chipmakers into partners instead of rivals and earned a little on each of a huge number of chips.
Every licensee also strengthened the platform: more chips meant more software, which brought more licensees.

image.label: A central node connected to many partner nodes
image.brief: 중심 노드 하나에 여러 파트너 노드가 연결된 네트워크 그래픽. 선이 점점 늘어나는 느낌.

head: Can someone else
carry your heavy assets?
body: The most valuable part of a business is not always the part that costs the most to build.
**Try it today:** list what you know that others would pay to use. Could you license it, teach it or partner on it instead of building everything yourself?

image.label: A single blueprint glowing on a dark desk
image.brief: 어두운 책상 위에서 홀로 빛나는 설계도 한 장.

factChecks.note: 1990년 11월 Acorn Computers, Apple, VLSI Technology의 합작으로 Advanced RISC Machines가 설립된 사실과 Acorn 출신 엔지니어 12명은 Arm 공식 연혁으로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1990년 11월 Acorn·Apple·VLSI 합작, Acorn 엔지니어 12명 확인.
초기 사무실이 케임브리지 인근의 개조한 헛간이었다는 이야기는 널리 전해지지만 회사 연혁과 James Ashton의 책으로 확인하세요. 카드에는 "reportedly"로 표시했습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 케임브리지셔의 헛간에서 시작 확인(Arm 공식).
초기 ARM 칩이 전원이 제대로 연결되지 않았는데도 작동했다는 일화는 전해지는 이야기입니다. 카드에는 "a story often told"로 표시했습니다.
Robin Saxby의 CEO 취임 시점(1991)과 Apple Newton의 Arm 칩 채택은 Arm 연혁 기준입니다. 확인하세요.
Texas Instruments가 Arm 설계를 휴대전화 칩에 쓰고 Nokia 휴대전화에 들어간 사실은 보도와 연혁 기준입니다. 특정 모델명은 넣지 않았습니다.
1998년 런던증권거래소·나스닥 동시 상장, 2016년 7월 SoftBank의 약 240억 파운드 인수 발표는 회사 및 SoftBank 보도자료로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1998년 4월 17일 런던 상장, 2016년 7월 SoftBank 약 243억 파운드 인수 확인.
2016년 무렵 연간 출하량은 "billions of chips a year"로만 적었고, 스마트폰 대부분에 쓰인다는 표현은 정성적으로 처리했습니다. 정확한 수치는 넣지 않았습니다.
